29 Light of wavelength 5.50  10–7
m from a laser is incident normally on a diffraction grating.
The diffracted light is incident on a semicircular screen, as shown in the view from above.
screen
diffraction grating
light,
wavelength 5.50  10–7 m
view from above
A total of 9 bright dots are formed on the screen.
The grating is at the centre of the semicircle. The lines of the grating are vertical. The separation
between adjacent lines in the grating is d.
What is a possible value of d ?
A
2.25  10–6
m
B
2.80  10–6
m
C
4.40  10–6
m
D
4.95  10–6
m

hints: Count the 9 dots as the zero order plus equal numbers on each side - what is the highest order $n$ visible on each side of the central dot?
Recall $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$ for normal incidence with $\lambda = 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, and that the semicircular screen collects all forward directions up to $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.
Require the highest visible order to have $\sin\theta \le 1$ while the next order has $\sin\theta > 1$, giving an inequality $n\lambda \le d < (n+1)\lambda$ to test.
walkthrough: A total of 9 dots means 1 central zero-order dot plus 4 dots on each side, so the maximum visible order is $n_{max} = 4$.
Use the grating equation for normal incidence: $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$ with $\lambda = 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
For $n=4$ to exist on the forward semicircle, $\sin\theta_4 = 4\lambda/d \le 1$, so $d \ge 4\lambda = 4 \times 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 2.20 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
For $n=5$ not to exist, $\sin\theta_5 = 5\lambda/d > 1$, so $d < 5\lambda = 5 \times 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 2.75 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Only $2.25 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ lies in this range. This is option A.

A.explanation: Satisfies $4\lambda \le d < 5\lambda$, so 4th order is visible but 5th order is not, giving 9 dots.

B.explanation: Gives $d/\lambda \approx 5.09$, so 5th order would exist and more than 9 dots would be seen.

C.explanation: Gives $d/\lambda = 8.0$, so orders up to $n=8$ would exist and far more than 9 dots would be seen.

D.explanation: Gives $d/\lambda = 9.0$, so orders up to $n=9$ would exist and far more than 9 dots would be seen.
